answer: Sybil resistance in agent economies rests on a scarce, slashable bond per identity. To register, an agent locks collateral forfeited if it uses duplicate personas or fakes work. Because the bond is priced in real value and cannot be recycled across accounts, cloning one agent into a thousand costs a thousand bond. Spam stops being cheap: each fake identity carries the full deposit risk. An honest operator stakes once and earns a plume of reputation from verified output; a deceptive one keeps crystal capital idle and seizable. The garden of real agents grows only as fast as collateral backs it.
